questions.q: What has to happen before LTV Global's design moves from 'approved with conditions' to simply 'approved'?
options: Both named conditions (LedgerPoint reconciliation load testing, Equipment Financing security audit) must be satisfied and documented
Nothing further; the conditions are symbolic only
The entire design must be rebuilt from scratch
A new Architecture Review Board must be convened with entirely different members
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that closing the conditions is real, necessary work — the design only becomes unconditionally approved once both the load test and the security audit are completed and documented.

questions.q: What would it mean if the LedgerPoint reconciliation load test revealed the reconciliation step can't keep pace with real volume?
options: A failure to be hidden from the client
Evidence that the whole single-org decision was wrong
A design gap caught before go-live rather than after, which is the entire point of the condition existing
Proof that LedgerPoint integration should be abandoned entirely
questions.explain: The lesson frames this possibility positively: catching a gap during the condition-closure testing, before go-live, is exactly what the condition was designed to enable.

questions.q: What does this capstone certify, per this lesson's closing section?
options: That the student is now a Salesforce Certified Technical Architect
The ability to produce a coherent, internally consistent, defensible architecture across major Technical Architect disciplines and defend it under live questioning — not the CTA credential itself
That the student has memorized every governor limit in the Salesforce platform
That LTV Global Industries is now a real, operating company
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly distinguishes practicing this reasoning from holding the actual CTA credential, which requires its own review board, scenario, and substantial professional experience this course doesn't substitute for.

questions.q: According to the full-course retrospective, how does the governance model (Lesson 22) connect back to the original Lesson 5 vision?
options: It has no connection to the vision statement
It only applies to the Equipment Financing business unit
It replaces the need for a Center of Excellence
It delivers the vision's 'sustainable governance' commitment by design (the Center of Excellence), rather than by hope
questions.explain: The retrospective explicitly ties the governance model back to the vision's commitment to governance that survives staff turnover, delivered through the CoE's standing, collective ownership rather than relying on any individual's memory.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the real, transferable skill the LTV Global scenario was built to practice?
options: The reasoning chain from requirement to decision to rejected alternative to honest justification, which applies beyond this specific fictional scenario
Memorizing the specific fictional facts about LTV Global Industries
The ability to draw entity-relationship diagrams quickly
Knowledge of Okta's specific configuration screens
questions.explain: The lesson closes by naming the transferable skill explicitly: the requirement-to-decision-to-rejected-alternative-to-defense reasoning pattern, not the specific (fictional) facts of LTV Global itself.
